newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline steady, surge in Nigeria demand seen.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline steady, surge in Nigeria demand seen.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Wednesday, with gasoline steady, gas oil softer and fuel oil unchanged, traders said.
Gasoline was little changed in price although traders were expecting a surge in Nigerian demand to scoop up some low octane barrels which have been languishing in the Med without buyers.
A Med refiner has already sold three high-RVP cargoes this month to traders and these were expected to move to West Africa.

High octane material is still tight and Italian demand is good. A refiner sold small a high octane cargo on Tuesday to an Italian buyer at $4 over the high of published quotes. The exact grade and timing of the material was not known.
Gas oil prices were slightly weaker but buying interest for diesel pegged premiums steady around $3-$4 over benchmark fob quotes. Traders said despite the enquiries trade was thin.
Trade for 0.2 percent sulphur material was also thin with the market valued around $3 a tonne under the diesel quotes.
Traders said firmer NWE markets especially for diesel could provide arbitrage opportunities but the mathematics for shipments elsewhere were still unworkable.
High sulphur cargoes were largely unchanged with one trader still heard offering a large piece out of Bilbao. Traders said he may move the material into the bunker market soon if it found no home.
Low sulphur was also unchanged with one seller seen on the marker out of Spain but little buying interest seen.
Traders said Italian demand remained subdued.
